findings.summary: The checked I1/V1 pair provides a strong static provenance-decision package: contract and initial manifest pin inputs/code; I1 fails closed because final outputs descend from pinned forbidden cached artifacts; V1 is admissible with required stages, declared-input ancestry, authorized writer, final hashes, metric extraction and positive-control pass.

The checked provenance-certificates V1 gate is not execution-identical to the realized-run V1 gate: certificate trace_id trace_18cc0e0b27 differs from run trace_id trace_15bbc3641e despite matching final hashes, write sequences and metrics, and the checked files contain no explicit bridge hash/pointer between those trace identities.

The checked V1 gate lacks the first-order ordered process/file event transcript and does not embed declared-input SHA-256 or contract/initial-manifest digests. Same-revision coexistence is therefore weaker than cryptographic run-to-contract binding, so full static predicate recomputation remains unresolved.
